tasks.subject: [community-member-erasure] [P1] Erase a member's account and messages on the Community server
tasks.description:
Build member erasure on the Community server (apps/community) and its shared wire (packages/shared/src/community-wire.ts). This is the hosted-community launch blocker. WHO MAY ERASE - The person, for one of their memberships (active or already left/removed) or for their whole account. Account erasure erases every membership on the host (listed at execution time, so memberships joined during the window are included), then deletes the account. - The current community owner, for a member who is no longer active (removed, left, or an imported historical member with user_id NULL). - Never an admin for someone else, never host authority (host operator session acting as host, host API key), never any bearer (connection grant, agent credential). All those get 403 FORBIDDEN. - Refusals: owner erasing their own active-owner membership -> 403 FORBIDDEN "Transfer ownership or delete the community first."; account erasure by a host_operators account -> 403; account erasure by the active owner of any community not in deletion_pending -> 409 STATE_CONFLICT naming those communities; owner erasing an active member or an already-erased member -> 409. - Reauthentication on every request: auth.api.verifyPassword when the account has a 'credential' account row; otherwise the session must be less than 5 minutes old, else 403 with new error code REAUTH_REQUIRED (add to CommunityWireErrorCodeSchema). Account form also requires confirmEmail equal to the account email exactly. WINDOW - Every request is 'scheduled' with execute_after = created_at + 72 hours (constant ERASURE_WINDOW_HOURS, not config). Nothing changes until it runs. Requester cancels (owner requests: the current owner). Cancel after execute_after -> 409. - Guards during an open erasure: ownership transfer to that member -> 409 "That member is leaving this community."; owner-claim redemption by an account with an open account erasure -> 409; an owner with an open account erasure cannot cancel their community's deletion -> 409 "Cancel your account deletion first." - Requests are accepted and erasures run in every lifecycle state: active, archived, held (when it exists), suspended, deletion_pending. MIGRATION (next free number at build time; the host-operator API spec takes 0012-0015), mirrored in src/schema.ts, added to src/migrate.ts: - erasure_requests(id uuid PK, kind IN ('membership','account'), requested_by IN ('self','owner'), user_id text NULL REFERENCES "user"(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, community_id uuid NULL REFERENCES communities(id), member_id uuid NULL, requested_by_member_id uuid NULL, parent_request_id uuid NULL REFERENCES erasure_requests(id), state IN ('scheduled','running','completed','cancelled'), execute_after, created_at, started_at, completed_at, cancelled_at, attempts int, next_attempt_at, last_error_class ~ '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$'). Checks: kind='account' => community_id and member_id NULL, requested_by='self', user_id set until the account row is deleted; kind='membership' => community_id and member_id set and user_id NULL (no completed request may link an account to a community); requested_by='owner' => requested_by_member_id set; execute_after >= created_at; timestamps match state. Composite tenant FKs (community_id, member_id) and (community_id, requested_by_member_id) -> members(community_id, id). Partial unique: one open (scheduled/running) membership request per (community_id, member_id, requested_by); one open account request per user_id. Due index on (next_attempt_at, execute_after) WHERE state IN ('scheduled','running'). - entry_redactions(id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PK, community_id, channel_id, entry_id, created_at), tenant FKs to channels and entries, index (channel_id, id). - entries.erased_at timestamptz NULL; members.erased_at timestamptz NULL; members.user_id DROP NOT NULL with check user_id IS NOT NULL OR erased_at IS NOT NULL OR (origin='imported' AND NOT active) -- if the import migration (origin column) has not landed, use user_id IS NOT NULL OR erased_at IS NOT NULL and the import migration widens it later; whichever lands second owns the combined check. - communities.content_version integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK > 0; export_archives.content_version integer NULL (NULL treated as 1). - deletion-worker.ts deletes the tenant's entry_redactions and erasure_requests rows before its members. PROCEDURE src/erasure.ts eraseMembership(communityId, memberId): idempotent by member id; every step locks communities row FOR UPDATE then the member row; batches of 500; every predicate names community_id. 1. End access: if active, run remove() from routes/members.ts with action 'member.erase.start'. Delete the member's connection_grants and connection_pairings rows, their agents' agent_credentials rows, agent_channel_members, owner_quota_windows, and for this community invite_uses / pending_admissions / admission_receipts for the member's user_id (read it before the husk step). Revoke the member's unexpired invites (keep rows). 2. Files: delete every attachments row uploaded by the member or their agents (bound or unbound); queueCommittedBlobDeletion, or discardManagedBlob for an uncommitted upload, in the same transaction. 3. Exports: mark every live export_archives row in the community deleted and queue its blob; increment communities.content_version. 4. Tombstones: entries of the member or their agents with erased_at IS NULL: text 'This message was erased.', author_display_name 'Erased member' / 'Erased agent', idempotency_key 'erased:'||id, payload_hash = SHA-256 of JSON {text:'This message was erased.',mentions:[],parentEntryId,attachmentIds:[]}, erased_at now(); delete their entry_mentions rows; insert one entry_redactions row each; increment content_version. Keep id, seq, channel_id, parent_entry_id, thread_root_entry_id, created_at, author ids. 5. Mentions: other entries in the community with an entry_mentions row for the member or their agents, or whose text contains one of their @handle tokens: delete those mention rows; rewrite every case-insensitive @ token (token ends at end of text or at a char not in [A-Za-z0-9_] and not a '.' or '-' followed by [A-Za-z0-9]; applies inside code and quotes too) to '@[erased]' via a pure exported rewriteHandleTokens(text, handles); do NOT change their payload_hash or idempotency_key; insert entry_redactions rows; increment content_version. 6. Seal (one transaction): repeat steps 3 and 5 for anything new, then husk: members display_name 'Erased member', handle 'erased-' + 12 random lowercase base32 chars, user_id NULL, active false, removed_at COALESCE(removed_at, now()), erased_at now(); re-key community_handles to the new handle (old one released); each owned agent display_name 'Erased agent', random erased- handle (and community_handles row), local_agent_id NULL, active false, revoked_at COALESCE. Tenant audit row 'member.erase.complete' (actor_kind 'system', subject_id husk id, nothing else). Log exactly {"event":"community.member_erased","communityId","memberId"}. The old handle must remain in members.handle until step 6 so a restart can still rewrite tokens. - Owner in a deletion_pending community (account erasure only): run only the husk (name, handle, user_id NULL, erased_at), keep role and active as the owner-lifecycle trigger requires, skip steps 2-5; the tenant deletion removes the rest. eraseAccount(userId): create one child membership request per members row with that user_id (parent_request_id, execute_after now()), run each, then in one transaction delete invite_uses for the user, pending_admissions and admission_receipts with account_id = user, verification rows whose identifier is the email, and the "user" row (session and account cascade). Log {"event":"community.account_erased","userId"}. Audit actions: member.erase.request, member.erase.cancel, member.erase.complete (ids and action names only). WORKER src/erasure-worker.ts started from main.ts beside the deletion worker: poll every 30s, claim one due request (state scheduled/running, execute_after <= now(), next_attempt_at <= now()) FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, mark running, run, mark completed; on failure store error class, attempts++, existing cleanup backoff. Clock injectable for tests. EXPORTS routes/exports.ts: owner export member query becomes LEFT JOIN "user" (email null for husks; coordinate with host-operator phase 4, which makes the same change and makes email nullable in CommunityExportManifestV1Schema: whichever lands first does both). Store communities.content_version read in the snapshot transaction on export_archives.content_version; at commit under the community lock refuse with 409 STATE_CONFLICT "The community changed while this export was being made. Try again." and discard the blob if it moved. ROUTES (new src/routes/erasures.ts; account routes on hostApi beside /memberships, session only; owner routes on communityApi): - GET /api/v1/account/erasures: open requests and ones cancelled in the last 30 days; membership items include communityName. - POST /api/v1/account/erasures: {kind:'membership', communityId, password?} | {kind:'account', confirmEmail, password?} -> 201 {erasure}; repeat while open -> 200 with the open one. - POST /api/v1/account/erasures/:id/cancel -> 200 {erasure}. - GET /api/v1/communities/:communityId/owner/former-members?cursor=: owner only, inactive members (id, displayName, handle, removedAt, origin, open erasure), 50 per page. - POST /api/v1/communities/:communityId/owner/erasures {memberId, password?}; GET .../owner/erasures; POST .../owner/erasures/:id/cancel (owner-made only). - GET /api/v1/communities/:communityId/channels/:id/redactions?cursor=&limit= (and single-community alias): same authorization as channel history; oldest first, max 100; each item {entry: current CommunityWireEntry projection}; cursor signed via encodeCursor with a kind:'redaction' field over entry_redactions.id; foreign cursor -> 410. Wire (strict): CommunityWireErasureSchema {id, kind, requestedBy, state, communityId|null, communityName|null, memberId|null, executeAfter, createdAt, completedAt|null, cancelledAt|null}; request schemas; CommunityWireRedactionPageQuerySchema {cursor?, limit? 1-100}; CommunityWireRedactionPageSchema {redactions: [{entry}] max 100, nextCursor|null}. Do NOT change CommunityWireEntrySchema or CommunityWireEventSchema, add no SSE event type, do not bump channel epochs. CLI: src/erasure-reapply.ts + package script erasure:reapply reading 'member ' and 'account ' lines from stdin, running with the web service stopped, printing counts only. BROWSER (writing-for-humans copy; every flow states what erasure cannot reach): - Manage.tsx: 'Erase your messages here' panel for non-owners: 'In 72 hours, we'll remove your name, messages, files, and your agents' messages from {community}. Your messages stay in their place in conversations, marked "This message was erased." You can cancel until then. We can't reach copies people already downloaded, or copies on members' computers that are offline.' Fields: community name, password. Owners see 'Transfer ownership or delete the community before you erase your messages here.' Banner while scheduled: 'Your messages here will be erased on {date}. Cancel'. - CommunityChooser.tsx (host root): 'Delete your account' panel ('In 72 hours, we'll delete your account on this host and erase your name, messages, files, and agents from every community here, including ones you left. You can cancel until then by signing in.' plus the cannot-reach sentence), email + password; replaced by 'You own {names}. Transfer ownership or delete them first.' for owners; list of scheduled erasures with Cancel; erase entry for communities already left. - CommunityAdministration.tsx: 'Former members' list with Erase -> confirm 'Erase {name}'s messages? In 72 hours, we'll remove their name, messages, files, and agents' messages from this community. Do this when they ask you to. You can cancel until then.' + password. DOCS: docs/guides/communities.mdx 'Export or leave' section; self-hosting docs (host operators cannot erase for a person; offline password recovery for someone who cannot sign in; erasure:reapply after a backup restore); changelog fragment in changelog/unreleased/; update specs/community-host-operator-api/02-specification.md Open Question 7 to point at this spec and list erasure as allowed while held. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (integration tests on real PostgreSQL and the filesystem BlobStore via tenancy-test-harness.ts; each test has a purpose comment): - AC-1 residue scan: seed person P (name 'Zephyrine Quill', email zq-canary@example.test, installation 'zq-canary-laptop', agent 'ZQ Canary Bot' with local id zq-canary-local, posts with canary-text-1, an agent post with canary-text-2, a reply in another thread, attachment zq-canary.txt with bytes canary-bytes-1, an unbound upload, idempotency key zq-canary-key) in communities A and B; member Q posts '@

thanks', a mention of P's agent, and a code block with '@

'; Q and the owner each make an export. The scan enumerates every public table and every text/varchar/text[]/json/jsonb column from information_schema.columns (never a hand list), every BlobStore object, captured log output, and the SHA-256 hex of each of P's entry payloads. Control: before erasure every canary is found in its expected place, else fail. After P erases membership in A (worker and blob sweep done): no canary in any A row, A blob, or log (except AC-10's named leftovers); B keeps every canary. After account deletion: no canary anywhere on the host; user/session/account/verification rows gone. - AC-2 thread shape: ids, seq, parent, thread root, created_at unchanged; history returns tombstone text, 'Erased member'/'Erased agent', mentions [], attachments []; parses with unchanged strict schema; Q's reply and thread query still work; page and live-stream cursors taken before still work (no 410). - AC-3 mentions: Q's texts read '@[erased] thanks', code block '@[erased]', agent mention '@[erased]'; no entry_mentions row targets P or P's agent; Q's retry of the original post with its original key and payload returns 200; a new member can take P's old handle and '@' resolves only to them. - AC-4 files/exports: P's blobs gone, GET /attachments/:id 404; both pre-erasure exports 404 and blobs gone; an export snapshotted before and committed after (test hook) is refused 409 and leaves no blob; a later owner export has P's husk with email null and no canary. - AC-5 window: executeAfter = createdAt + 72h; full-table digest of A equal before request and just before execution; P can still post; cancel leaves digest equal; cancel after executeAfter 409; worker never runs a cancelled request. - AC-6 authority: 403 for host API key, host operator as host, grant bearer, agent bearer, admin on another member, member on another member; owner on active member 409; owner self 403; account deletion 403 for host operator, 409 for owner of an active community; cross-cancel refused both ways. - AC-7 guards: transfer to P 409; owner claim by P's account 409; owner with open account erasure cannot cancel community deletion 409; a membership joined during an account window is erased. - AC-8 crash/repeat: kill after each step 1-6 via test hook, restart, same final digest as an uninterrupted run; eraseMembership twice and reapply after completion change nothing; person + owner requests on one membership both complete with one erasure. - AC-9 lifecycles: completes when A is archived, held (if present), suspended, deletion_pending; in a deletion_pending community P owns, account erasure husks the owner row and the tenant deletion removes the rest. - AC-10 named leftovers asserted explicitly: a free-text display name typed by another member remains; audit rows hold the husk id. Owner can erase an imported historical member (if import exists) and a member who left before this shipped. - AC-11 redaction feed: empty before; after, one item per changed entry with current projection, strict-schema valid; 404 for a channel the caller cannot read; cursor from another channel 410. - AC-12 backup: snapshot DB + BlobStore, erase P, restore, run erasure:reapply with the logged ids: AC-1 scan passes again and P's restored account is deleted. - Unit: rewriteHandleTokens (., -, _, trailing punctuation, case, prefix handles like zq vs zq2, code, quotes); tombstone payload hash; reauth rule (password account; OAuth-only with fresh and stale session). Browser tests: each flow shows the cannot-reach sentence; owner sees the transfer message; cancel updates the banner. Migration test: old code against new schema, and the user-presence check under both orders with the import migration. Backout: before any erasure ran, revert code and keep the migration; after one ran, forward-fix only (old owner export inner-joins "user" and would drop husks).

tasks.subject: [community-member-erasure] [P2] Replace cached copies of erased Community messages in DorkOS
tasks.description:
Make DorkOS installations drop their cached copies of erased Community messages (apps/server, packages/db). Depends on the Community server exposing GET /api/v1/communities/:communityId/channels/:id/redactions?cursor=&limit= returning CommunityWireRedactionPageSchema {redactions: [{entry: CommunityWireEntry}] (max 100, oldest first), nextCursor: cursor|null}. Not a host launch blocker: it reaches copies on members' own machines. The server writes entry_redactions from its first erasure, so this catches up on every earlier erasure.

WHY: apps/server/src/services/communities/remote/mirror-store.ts keeps a persisted mirror (community_mirror_entries, room_entries, and an external author record in authors with the display name) and importEntry never updates an entry it already has. DorkOS message search (apps/server/src/services/search/registry.ts roomsSource, row-frontier.ts) indexes room_entries above a per-room watermark and assumes rows only append, so an in-place edit is never re-indexed.

BUILD:
- @dorkos/db migration: community_room_mirrors gains redaction_cursor text NULL.
- Remote subscription runtime (remote-room-subscription-runtime.ts / remote-community-adapter.ts): after every replay_complete and every 15 minutes while subscribed, page the redaction feed for each mirrored room from the stored cursor, using the pinned origin and the connection grant like history reads. Validate with the strict schema.
- For each item whose entry exists in community_mirror_entries, in one SQLite transaction: update room_entries.body ({text}) and mentions; update community_mirror_entries.entry_json, author_display_name, author_kind; if the entry text is the tombstone 'This message was erased.' and author name is 'Erased member' or 'Erased agent', set that external author's display name in authors to the same. Store the new cursor. Items for entries not in the mirror are skipped (the cursor still advances).
- Never dispatch a local agent for a redaction; it is not a new post and must not go through RoomEntryWriter or the dispatch claim.
- After a page that changed rows, drop that room's search frontier so the room is re-indexed from the start; add a per-container invalidation to the frontier store (apps/server/src/services/search/frontier-store.ts) if none fits.
- A 404 from the feed marks that connection as not supporting redactions until restart, logged once; nothing else changes.
- Changelog fragment in changelog/unreleased/.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- AC-13: a DorkOS test server paired to a real community server (community test harness) mirrors a channel where P posted canary-text-1 and Q mentioned P, and indexes it. Control: a scan of every table and column in the local SQLite file (enumerated from sqlite_master and pragma table_info, never a hand list) and a message search for canary-text-1 both find the canary. After P's erasure runs on the community server and one feed sync: neither the SQLite scan nor search finds any canary; mirrored entries show 'This message was erased.' and Q's '@[erased]'; the external author reads 'Erased member'; no local agent was dispatched.
- Against a community server without the route (404): one log line, no change, no retry loop.
- Restart mid-page resumes from the stored cursor and ends in the same state.
- Unit: applying the same redaction page twice is a no-op; a redaction for an entry not in the mirror advances the cursor only.
